rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know God may fall silent from awe rather than incapacity; afterward they hasten to good works, consider themselves deficient, and never regard their deeds as enough to claim merit.
rows.anchor: ألم تعلموا أن لله عبادا أسكتتهم خشية من غير عي ولا بكم

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Job says God plants wisdom through mercy in the hearts of young and old; wisdom appears on the tongue, does not depend on age or experience, and a wise child retains honor among sages.
rows.anchor: فقال أيوب: إن الله سبحانه يزرع الحكمة بالرحمة في قلب الصغير والكبير

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Job rebukes his three visitors for presuming his suffering proves their righteousness; if they examined themselves, they would find faults hidden by their own health and prosperity.
rows.anchor: ثم أقبل أيوب على الثلاثة فقال: أتيتموني غضابا

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Job laments losing his former standing and asks why God created him, wishing he had died at birth or could know which sin caused God's favor to turn away.
rows.anchor: ثم أعرض عنهم وأقبل على ربه مستعينا به متضرعا إليه فقال: رب لأي شيء خلقتني؟

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Job recalls sheltering strangers, supporting the poor, protecting orphans, and caring for widows, asking whether death would have been better than his present loss of voice and status.
rows.anchor: ألم أكن للغريب دارا وللمسكين قرارا ولليتيم وليا وللأرملة قيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job's continuing lament recounts severe bodily deterioration, inability to eat or walk, loss of property and children, and abandonment by relatives, friends, servants, and former dependents.
rows.anchor: تقطعت أصابعي فإني لأرفع الأكلة من الطعام بيدي جميعا فما تبلغان فمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job says he longs for his awe of God to be removed and his speech released so he could defend himself, since God sees and hears him yet has not drawn near to relieve him.
rows.anchor: ثم كان ينبغي للعبد أن يحاج عن نفسه، لرجوت أن يعافيني عند ذلك مما بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cloud covers Job and his companions; God tells Job to rise and plead his case, then challenges him to perform impossible feats, such as controlling a lion, measuring light, or returning yesterday.
rows.anchor: فلما قال ذلك أيوب وأصحابه أظله غمام حتى ظن أصحابه أنه عذاب، ثم نودي منه: يا أيوب إن الله يقول: ها أنا دنوت منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine challenge points to God's creation and governance of earth, sky, seas, mountains, rain, clouds, thunder, lightning, snow, day, night, trees, light, and wind as beyond Job's knowledge or power.
rows.anchor: أردت أن تخاصمني بفيك أم أن تحاجني بخطابك أم أردت ان تكابرني بضعفك؟ أين أنت مني يوم خلقت الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether Job assigned reason to humans, hearing to creatures, dominion to angels, or provision and maternal care to animals; their instincts and livelihoods display divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: ومن جعل العقول في الرجال؟ ومن شق الأسماع؟ ومن ذلت الملائكة لملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine challenge asks whether Job knows the roar of thunder, source of lightning, depths of the sea, or hidden stores of snow, day, night, light, and wind.
rows.anchor: هل تدري ما أصوات الرعود أم من أى شيء لهب البرق؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine speech invokes enormous beasts and a fire-breathing sea dragon, asking whether Job can restrain, feed, measure, or command them; their scale underscores human incapacity before God's creation.
rows.anchor: أتطيق غضبه حين يغضب أم تأمره فيطيعك؟ تبارك الله وتعالى.

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Job confesses that he cannot meet God's challenge, acknowledges God's deeds exceed even those described, and says he spoke only to seek pardon and mercy; he covers his mouth, submits, and asks forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فقال أيوب: قصرت عن هذا الأمر الذي يعرض على ليت الأرض انشقت

rows.speaker: الله سبحانه
rows.claim: God says his prior knowledge encompassed Job and his mercy preceded wrath; he forgives Job, restores his household and property doubled as a sign and lesson, and directs him to strike the ground for healing water.
rows.anchor: يا أيوب فقد نفذ فيك علمي وسبقت رحمتي غضبي إذ خطئت فقد غفرت لك

rows.speaker: الله سبحانه
rows.claim: God orders Job to offer a sacrifice for his companions and seek their forgiveness because they sinned in their treatment of him.
rows.anchor: وقرب عن صحابتك قربانا واستغفر لهم فإنهم قد عصوني فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job strikes the ground, bathes in the spring, and is cured; his wife returns, recognizes him by his smile, and embraces him. Ibn Abbas says their property and children passed before them before the embrace ended.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فو الذي نفس عبد الله بيده ما فارقته من عناقه حتى مر بهما كل مال لهما وولد

words: وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī links the account to the Qur'anic statement that Job called upon his Lord because harm had touched him.
rows.anchor: فذلك قوله وأيوب إذ نادى ربه أني مسني الضر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet's report that Job endured illness for eighteen years, abandoned by near and distant kin except two visiting brothers; one brother wrongly inferred that such a long illness proved grave sin.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن أيوب نبي الله لبث به بلاؤه ثماني عشرة سنة، فرفضه القريب والبعيد إلا رجلين من إخوانه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the same report, Job says God knew he used to reconcile disputants who invoked Him, then return home and atone so they would mention God only truthfully; Thaʿlabī gives no grading.
rows.anchor: فقال أيوب: ما أدري ما يقولان غير أن الله سبحانه يعلم أني كنت أمر بالرجلين يتنازعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaʿlabī notes that scholars differ over when Job prayed, why he said harm had touched him, and how long his ordeal lasted.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء في وقت ندائه، والسبب الذي قال: لأجله أني مسني الضر وفي مدة بلائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing Anas's report from the Prophet, Job's wife held his hand when he went out; after the healing revelation she met him restored, and two clouds poured gold and silver into his wheat and barley threshing floors.
rows.anchor: فكان يخرج بحاجته فإذا قضى حاجته أمسكت امرأته بيده حتى يبلغ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Job lay on a refuse heap for seven years and some months while animals passed over him.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: مكث أيوب مطروحا على كناسة في مزبلة لبني إسرائيل سبع سنين وأشهرا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Job had no ordinary ulcer; something like a woman's breast protruded from him and then burst.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: لم يكن بأيوب أكلة إنما كان يخرج منه مثل ثدي النساء ثم يتفقأ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says only Job's patient wife remained to serve him; Job never ceased remembering and praising God and patiently bearing the trial, which left Iblis distressed.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: ولم يبق له مال ولا ولد ولا صديق ولا أحد يقربه غير رحمة صبرت معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says he stripped Job of wealth, children, and health without making him less patient or grateful; his followers advise exploiting Job's wife, and Iblis approaches her in disguise to recall their former prosperity.
rows.anchor: أعياني هذا العبد الذي سألت ربي أن يسلطني على ماله وولده

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: In al-Hasan's account, Iblis gives Job's wife a lamb and claims slaughtering it will cure Job; she urges Job to sacrifice it and complains of their lost health, wealth, children, and friends.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: فصرخت، فلما صرخت علم أن قد جزعت، فأتاها بسخلة

rows.speaker: أيوب
rows.claim: Job identifies the tempter as God's enemy, contrasts eighty years of blessing with seven years and months of trial, and says fairness requires patience for an equal span; he rejects an offering to anyone but God, vows one hundred lashes if healed, and expels his wife.
rows.anchor: قال أيوب: أتاك عدو الله فنفخ فيك وأجبته؟! ويلك أرأيت ما تبكين عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: After his wife leaves and he has no food, Job prostrates and prays that harm has touched him; God answers, and two springs heal him, one by bathing and one by drinking.
rows.anchor: خر ساجدا وقال: رب مسني الضر ثم رد ذلك إلى ربه فقال وأنت أرحم الراحمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job finds his family and wealth restored in doubled measure; gold locusts fall from his bathwater, and he gathers them as God's blessing before his wife returns to search for him.
rows.anchor: فجعل يلتفت فلا يرى شيئا مما كان له من أهل ومال إلا وقد أضعفه الله له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Job summons his wife, reveals his identity, and says that he obeyed God rather than Satan and prayed, so God restored what she sees.
rows.anchor: قال: وهابت صاحب الحلة أن تأتيه فتسأله عنه، فأرسل إليها أيوب فدعاها فقال: ما تريدين يا أمة الله؟

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says Job's ordeal lasted seven years.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: كان أيوب في بلائه سبع سنين

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb gives a different duration: Job's ordeal lasted exactly three years, not a day longer.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: لبث أيوب في ذلك البلاء ثلاث سنين لم يزد يوما واحدا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Satan appeared to Job's wife in a magnificent form, claimed to be earth's god, and offered to restore her family and possessions if Job bowed to him; he showed her their apparent belongings.
rows.anchor: فلما غلب أيوب إبليس ولم يستطع منه شيئا اعترض امرأته في هيئة ليس كهيئة بني آدم

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb also heard that Satan suggested Job could be cured simply by eating without invoking God's name; Thaʿlabī adds that God knows best.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: وقد سمعت أنه إنما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another book says Satan offered Rahma restoration if she bowed once; Job recognized the plot, sought God's help, and again vowed to strike her one hundred times if cured.
rows.anchor: ورأيت في بعض الكتب أن إبليس قال لرحمة: وإن شئت فاسجدي لي سجدة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has mercy on Job's wife for patiently remaining with him and provides a way to release Job from his oath: he should strike her once with a bundle of twigs, as in 38:44.
rows.anchor: قالوا: ثم الله سبحانه رحم رحمة امرأة أيوب بصبرها معه على البلاء

rows.speaker: وهب وغيره
rows.claim: Wahb and others say Job's wife earned food for him; when work dried up, she sold a lock of her hair for bread, and he then said that harm had touched him.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب وغيره: كانت امرأة أيوب تكسب له وتعمل للناس وتجيئه بقوته، فلما طال عليهما البلاء

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say Job spoke when worms approached his heart and tongue and he feared becoming unable to remember and reflect.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إنما قال: مسني الضر حين قصدت الدود إلى قلبه ولسانه فخشي أن يعيى عن الذكر والفكر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says two brothers condemned Job's trial from a distance, and their accusation hurt him more than any bodily affliction; he then testified to his charity before God.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير: كان لأيوب أخوان فأتياه فقاما من بعيد لا يقدران أن يدنوا منه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: In that report Job asks God to confirm he never knowingly slept full while someone was hungry or owned two shirts while someone was naked; God confirms it as the brothers listen.
rows.anchor: اللهم إن كنت تعلم أني لم أبت ليلة شبعان وأنا أعلم مكان جائع فصدقني فصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Job spoke because enemies gloated over his suffering; a report says he later named their gloating as the hardest part of the ordeal.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه: مسني الضر من شماتة الأعداء، يدل عليه ما روي أنه قيل له بعد ما عوفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says a worm fell from Job's thigh; he returned it, accepting that God had made him its food, but its bite hurt more than all the other worms.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال ذلك حين وقعت دودة من فخذه فرفعها وردها إلى موضعها

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم جنيد
rows.claim: Al-Junayd reads Job's words as presenting his need in the act of asking so that God may bestow from His generosity.
rows.anchor: وسمعت أبا عبد الله بن محمد بن جعفر الأبيوردي يقول: سمعت أبا عبد الله محمد بن عباد البغدادي يقول: سئل أبو القاسم جنيد عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم بن حبيب
rows.claim: Ibn Habib argues Job's words are a supplication, not a complaint: God's response follows a prayer, as shown by the text saying God answered him; the gathering accepts this reading.
rows.anchor: وسمعت أستاذنا أبا القاسم بن حبيب يقول: حضرت مجلسا غاصا بالفقهاء والأدباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A preceding account concludes that the man who promised never to disobey God died that night; people called him Dhul-Kifl and found a written notice that God had forgiven him.
rows.anchor: والله لا أعصي الله أبدا، فمات من ليلته فقيل مات ذو الكفل، فوجدوا على باب داره مكتوبا

rows.speaker: نبي من الأنبياء
rows.claim: An al-Aʿmash report relayed from ʿAbd Allah al-Harith describes a prophet asking for someone to fast by day, pray by night, and not grow angry; a seemingly unimpressive youth accepts after being asked three times.
rows.anchor: وروى الأعمش عن المنهال بن عمرو عن عبد الله بن الحرث أن نبيا من الأنبياء قال: من يكفل لي

rows.speaker: نبي من الأنبياء
rows.claim: After the prophet dies, the youth judges in his place; Satan tries to provoke him through a persistent complainant, but the youth follows the man personally and is not angered, hence the name Dhul-Kifl.
rows.anchor: فسمي ذا الكفل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says al-Yasaʿ sought a successor whom he could observe during his own lifetime and required daytime fasting, night prayer, and freedom from anger; a young man repeatedly volunteers and is appointed.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لما كبر اليسع (عليه السلام) قال: لو أني استخلفت رجلا على الناس يعمل عليهم في حياتي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In Mujahid's account, Iblis sends devils against the successor, then appears as an old wronged man at his midday rest and spins out a complaint over successive days until the judge loses his nap.
rows.anchor: فجعل إبليس يقول للشياطين: عليكم بفلان فأعياهم فقال: دعوني وإياه فأتاه في صورة شيخ فقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one called Dhul-Nun in the verse is Jonah, whom the passage depicts calling himself the sinful, runaway servant.
rows.anchor: فقام يونس فقال: أنا الرجل العاصي والعبد الآبق، وألقى نفسه في الماء فجاء حوت فابتلعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah throws himself into the sea; a fish swallows him and a larger fish swallows that fish, while God commands the larger fish not to harm Jonah because its belly is his prison, not his food.
rows.anchor: وأوحى الله إلى الحوت: لا تؤذ منه شعرة فإني جعلت بطنك سجنه، ولم أجعله طعاما لك

rows.speaker: الآخرون
rows.claim: Others say Jonah left angry after God withheld the punishment he had promised his people; embarrassed to return seeming false, he did not know why their destruction had been averted.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخرون: بل ذهب عن قومه مغاضبا لربه إذ كشف عنهم العذاب بعد ما وعدهموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some accounts say Jonah feared his people would kill a prophet whose announced punishment failed to arrive, so he left without knowing why the punishment was diverted; the fuller account is in Surah Yunus.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار: إن قومه كان من عادتهم أن يقتلوا من جربوا عليه الكذب

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says the reciprocal form mufaʿala usually involves two parties but can describe one person's action; here مغاضبا means Jonah was angry and resentful.
rows.anchor: قال القتيبي: المغاضبة مفاعلة، وأكثر المفاعلة من اثنين كالمناظرة والمخاصمة والمجادلة

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi explains that Arabs use anaf, literally associated with the nose, for anger because the two are closely linked; Jonah resented that his people could call him a liar.
rows.anchor: والعرب تسمي الغضب أنفا، والأنف غضبا لقرب أحدهما من الآخر

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says Jonah had long endured his people and wished God's punishment would befall them; after the promised deadline passed without punishment, he left like a runaway slave.
rows.anchor: وكان من طول ما عاين وقاسى من بلاء قومه يشتهي أن ينزل الله بهم بأسه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan gives another account: Jonah was ordered to warn his people, sought time to prepare, was told the mission could not wait even for shoes, and left angrily at the haste.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : إنما غاضب ربه من أجل أنه أمر بالمصير إلى قومه لينذرهم بأسه
